articles.title: You can now play Silksong on flagship Android phones — and pick up where you left off on PC
articles.summary: Hollow Knight: Silksong hasn’t been ported to phones, but GameSir’s GameHub installs Proton and other components to let you emulate it beautifully.
articles.body: Hollow Knight: Silksong, one of the hottest games of the year with a reported five million players in its first week, didn’t launch on smartphones. But that won’t stop you from playing it on Android — because a new leap in Windows to Android emulation means you can easily install and run the Steam version on flagship phones like my Galaxy S25. I’m talking about GameHub, the app from Chinese mobile gamepad manufacturer GameSir, which just launched version 5.0 with two key features that help it rise above the Windows-on-phone emulation scene. [Media: First, it automatically configures itself with the right graphics drivers, translation layer, and other components when you launch the game — something that I spent hours trying to do manually with rivals Winlator, GameNative, and an earlier version of GameHub with far worse results. Second and just as importantly: it can sync your Steam savegames to and from your PC. The result: you can download this app, log into your Steam account, tap to install the game, tap to play the game, tap a couple more times to enable Steam cloud saves… and then you’re playing a Steam game on a phone! Follow these instructions and you can sync your save back to your PC as well. Is it worth it? On my vanilla Samsung Galaxy S25, this PC game really does feel playable on a phone, at least once I attach a USB-C gamepad with an integrated cooler like the GameSir X3 Pro I’m testing right now. I played over an hour yesterday and didn’t feel the need to pick up my Steam Deck instead. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: With a normal PS5 controller, I saw framerates anywhere between 50 and 120 frames per second at my phone’s full, widescreen native resolution — did I mention GameHub supports widescreen and HDR? — and it runs a bit better at 720p. But with the X3 Pro I was able to maintain framerates of over 100fps even in big fights, so long as I plugged the gamepad’s Peltier cooling plate and noisy fan into USB-C power. I guess I shouldn’t make fun of phone coolers anymore! [Image: Peltier cooler actually works, but fan is a bit annoying. It’s not as smooth as my Steam Deck or other handhelds without that added cooling: when my phone is thermally throttling, moments where it hits 50 or 60fps don’t feel like 50fps or 60fps, they feel like the game is borderline unplayable. But I was pleased to see the cooling solution do its job! I imagine a larger Galaxy phone, or a phone designed for gaming, or a dedicated Android handheld, would have an easier time. You probably won’t want to use a phone much weaker than the S25 for this quick-reflex game. When I tried GameHub and Silksong on an older Pixel 9 with a Tensor G4, it balanced on the knife’s edge of playability, and definitely fell off without a cooler attached. The Pixel 9 also doesn’t currently let me watch the game’s cutscenes, a bit of a dealbreaker if you’re buying the game to play on phone, though the Galaxy S25 plays cutscenes fine as of this latest GameHub release. [Image: I would not recommend playing Silksong with a touchscreen, but someone will surely beat it that way. Some in the Android emulation community have turned to the Nintendo Switch emulator Eden for better sustained performance in Silksong, and I’ve heard that one runs at a stable 120fps without extra cooling. But that would require somehow obtaining a downloadable copy of the Switch version of the game, and it might be difficult to transfer saves with a real Switch. With GameHub, I’m downloading my legitimately purchased games and saves from Steam itself. That’s amazing. [Image: [Image: Windows emulation on Android is looking like a game-changer. And Silksong is just one of the games it might be about to change. Today, that’s because this game requires an incredibly low amount of performance and power to play, but future phones might carve out more and more of the PC game library. Just don’t rely on GameHub too much yet. Even though many are enthusiastic about the big improvements in GameHub 5.0, others are complaining that it broke games that were previously working. It could be worth waiting for the dust to settle.

articles.title: 5 great indie games from GDC 2026
articles.summary: The 2026 GDC Festival of Gaming featured some cool indie titles like At Fate’s End, Mina the Hollower, and The Melty Way.
articles.body: I just got back from the GDC Festival of Gaming, a big industry-focused event in San Francisco that was formerly known as the Game Developers Conference. While the show is mostly about educational sessions and networking opportunities for working developers, there were also a bunch of games that I got to play. Here are some of my favorites, listed alphabetically. Best of all, these could all launch this year — hopefully well before Grand Theft Auto VI. At Fate’s End [Media: At Fate’s End is a gorgeous new action-adventure game from Spiritfarer developer Thunder Lotus all about grappling with sibling relationships through exploration and battles. I got to see two fights with just the first of the main character’s siblings. But even those early battles were thrilling skirmishes with dramatic animations, full-screen lightning attacks, and dialogue choices that can influence which ending you get. I haven’t been able to stop thinking about the game all week. At Fate’s End is set to launch in 2026 on PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X / S. Mina the Hollower [Media: The next title from Shovel Knight developer Yacht Club Games is an homage Link’s Awakening on the Game Boy, but with the twist that you play as a mouse that can dig through the ground. The game is set to launch sometime this spring following a delay last October, and based on a new demo I played, the extra time was worth it. I was disappointed by the demo I played on PC last year, but this time around, I loved exploring the game’s world, fighting challenging enemies, and even digging my way into some hidden secrets. Yacht Club Games plans to launch Mina the Hollower this spring on PC, PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, and Xbox Series X / S. The Melty Way [Media: The Melty Way blends challenging, Super Meat Boy-style platforming with a gooey twist: You play as an adorable little slime, and as you move through the world, you melt away and get smaller. Becoming smaller gives you advantages like higher jumps and being able to squeeze into tighter pathways. But if you don’t find a checkpoint or finish the level in time, your little slime will die — and the slime is so dang cute that you’ll feel bad for letting that happen. The Melty Way is launching in early access on Steam on April 24th. Poke a Nose [Image: In Poke a Nose, from developer Jelle van Meerendonk, you fly around as a severed hand that collects toilet paper and finishes levels by poking noses. The concept is absurd, yet flying around as a hand actually takes some finesse, so getting a finger into a nose at the end of a level feels like a satisfying accomplishment. It’s targeting a 2026 release on PC, though van Meerendonk tells The Verge that early 2027 is “more likely.” Super Meat Boy 3D [Media: Speaking of Super Meat Boy, Super Meat Boy 3D feels like a promising 3D version of the brutally difficult 2D platformer. I was happy to see that a lot of the hallmarks of the original are present, like really floaty jumps and buzzsaws littered around the world. Sometimes, I fell to an untimely death because the new perspective led to some confusing jumps, but restarts were quick, so I didn’t mind too much. Super Meat Boy 3D is coming out in 2026 on PC, PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, and Xbox Series X / S.

articles.title: Amazon Discounts Upcoming MTG Star Trek Boosters and Major Marvel Sets for Prime Day
articles.summary: Score huge Prime Day savings on Magic: The Gathering, including 19% off Star Trek Play Boosters preorders, discounted Marvel precons, Hobbit collector items, and a whole lot more.
articles.body:
Whether you’re new to Magic: The Gathering or have been playing for years, it’s an expensive hobby. And while it’s always “just one more booster pack” or “one more Commander Deck”, finding great Magic deals helps build out a collection for a little less.

Thankfully, Prime Day has arrived, and it’s packed with Magic deals across bundles, Commander decks, and Play Booster boxes, whether you’re looking for Universes Beyond or something true to Magic’s ever-evolving lore.

Kicking things off with the humble Play Booster, we’ve seen a bunch of great deals - including one on the Star Trek set. Yes, the Star Trek set that doesn’t launch until next month.

Right now, Amazon is offering a 19% discount on a Play Booster box from the upcoming set, bringing it down to $170.61 for 30 packs.

It’s not just Picard and pals, either. Secrets of Strixhaven was probably my favorite set of this year so far, and you can pick up a Play Booster Box for $134.94 - an 18% discount from the MSRP of $164.70.

After the disappointment of Marvel’s Spider-Man, I was pleased to see that Marvel Super Heroes is a much better set, and you can save 28% on a Play Booster box . It’s $147.95 instead of $209.70.

Finally, Universes Beyond: The Hobbit sees Magic return to Middle-Earth, and you can save 23% on a Play Booster box there, too. It’s $161.99 instead of $211.11 , and you get yourself a box topper.

It’s worth noting that Play Boosters are much, much less likely to contain the more valuable cards in any given set. Instead, you’ll need to opt for more expensive Collector Boosters, but those can be like gold dust.

There are some discounted bundles that can net you a Collector Booster, though. The Marvel Super Heroes Gift Bundle includes 9 Play Boosters and a Collector Booster, and you can save $10 right now , bringing it down to just shy of $80.

If you’re not fussed by the Collector Booster, the Marvel Super Heroes Bundle is discounted by a much bigger 27% , bringing it down to just over $50 for those Play Boosters and some extra goodies.

Another option is Draft Night, with the Marvel one discounted by 25% . It includes 12 Play Boosters to play sealed Magic with, and a Collector Booster for the winner, but we won’t tell if you just buy the box for yourself. And at $89.99, we crunched the numbers - you’re basically getting the Collector Booster for $6.

More into Turtles than Superheroes? The Magic x Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Pizza bundle includes 9 Play Boosters and a Collector Booster. It’s dropped from $99.99 down to $89.99 - radical!

Lastly, for bundles, the Starter Collection is a great way to get yourself a bundle of cards that are standard-legal for you to build your own decks with, and it’s down to $51.79 from $59.99 . It includes over 350 cards, and you’ll get three Play Boosters for good measure, too.

Commander is Magic’s most popular format by a country mile, and what helps keep it ticking over is the regular cadence of new preconstructed decks you can play right out of the box, tear apart to make your own, or use to kick off a regular Commander night with friends.

Blight Curse is a fantastic precon from Lorwyn Eclipsed earlier this year, and it’s seeing a 30% discount . That brings it from $49.99 down to $34.95, although I’d caution newcomers against picking it up, as it’s not the most straightforward playstyle.

Instead, consider Avengers Assemble. This Marvel Super Heroes precon is packed with familiar faces and is a great deck to learn to play the Commander format with. It’s $54.90, down from $74.99 .

Sticking with Marvel precons, the Fantastic Four one is seeing a price drop to $44.99. Amazon has that at a 17% discount , but given the MSRP is actually $74.99, it’s a steeper drop than that. Doom Prevails, which is all about Marvel villains, is down to $67.38 - a roughly 10% discount.

Finally, the Fallout Commander Decks were pretty great and full of flavor for anyone who loves the long-running RPG series, and the S.C.I.E.N.C.E. precon is under $50 . It’s not the easiest for newcomers to get started with, but if you want a piece of the Wasteland in your Magic collection, this is a good way to get it.

Lloyd Coombes is an experienced freelancer in tech, gaming and fitness seen at Polygon, Eurogamer, Macworld, TechRadar and many more. He's a big fan of Magic: The Gathering and other collectible card games, much to his wife's dismay.

articles.title: In 1991, Nintendo used special cartridges for its Campus Challenge and later destroyed all but one; the survivor reached a New York garage sale in 2006 and resold on eBay for $20,100 three years later
articles.summary: It looked like an odd old Nintendo cartridge sitting among boxes of gaming memorabilia.
articles.body: It looked like an odd old Nintendo cartridge sitting among boxes of gaming memorabilia. But when video-game collector Rob Walters came across it at a New York garage sale in 2006, he had stumbled upon something that Nintendo had never intended to become a collector's treasure.The cartridge was made specifically for Nintendo's 1991 Campus Challenge, a nationwide gaming competition that took place at around 60 US college campuses and other locations. It combined three Nintendo games into a single custom cartridge: Super Mario Bros. 3, PinBot and Dr. Mario.Guinness World Records now lists the cartridge as the rarest Super Mario videogame, recording its 2009 sale for $20,100. According to Guinness, Nintendo destroyed the Campus Challenge cartridges after the tournament, except for one that had been retained by a Nintendo employee and eventually sold to Walters at the 2006 garage sale.A special cartridge built for competitionNintendo created the 1991 Campus Challenge as a follow-up to its hugely successful 1990 Nintendo World Championships. Instead of travelling primarily to major cities, the new competition brought Nintendo gaming to college campuses and spring-break destinations.According to the 2009 NintendoAGE eZine, the tour visited around 60 college campuses, with thousands of students competing for a chance to reach the national championship. The final competition took place in Orlando in January 1992, where Steven Lucas was crowned the National Champion for 1991.The custom cartridge was central to the competition. Players began with Super Mario Bros. 3, where they had to collect 25 coins. They then moved to PinBot and needed to reach 100,000 points before progressing to Dr. Mario. The combined score determined the competitor's result.Unlike a normal Nintendo game, the cartridge was never designed for sale in stores. It contained specially modified versions of the games and included hardware for the tournament setup. The cartridge even had a phone jack, which was used to transmit player scores and names to a central computer. Those scores could then be displayed on a large screen behind the contestants.Nintendo tried to make the cartridges disappearOnce the competition ended, the custom cartridges had little practical purpose outside Nintendo's events. The NintendoAGE investigation published in 2009 said almost all of the cartridges were physically destroyed after the contest. The article reported that only one had been discovered at that point. It also noted that the person who ran the contest believed as many as three or four might have survived, meaning “only one known to exist” is more precise than saying only one was ever made.The surviving cartridge was eventually traced to a former Nintendo employee. In May 2006, photographs of a large collection of Nintendo competition cartridges appeared online. One unusual NES cartridge initially confused collectors because of its strange hardware and phone connection. When it was powered on and examined, its game list revealed what it really was: the 1991 Nintendo Campus Challenge cartridge.The $1,000 garage sale haulWalters' discovery was even more extraordinary because the Campus Challenge cartridge was not the only Nintendo rarity he found that day. PriceCharting's account of the garage sale says Walters stopped at the New York sale in August 2006 and discovered a collection belonging to a former Nintendo employee. Among the items were a 1990 Nintendo World Championships cartridge, the 1991 Campus Challenge cartridge, a 1992 Campus Challenge cartridge and other Nintendo promotional material.The seller told Walters he had previously worked for Nintendo and did not want the items publicly identified. Walters eventually paid $1,000 for the collection. PriceCharting later estimated the collection's value at more than $50,000.The Campus Challenge cartridge alone would eventually account for a substantial portion of that value.From $14,000 to $20,100Walters later sold the 1991 Campus Challenge cartridge privately to collector J.J. Hendricks for $14,000 in July 2009. Hendricks did not hold on to it for long. Just three months later, he put the cartridge on eBay with a starting bid of 99 cents and no reserve. According to an interview with Hendricks published by RetroGaming with Racketboy, the price remained at about $8,500 until the final minutes. Then a burst of late bidding pushed the final price to $20,100.Guinness World Records records the same $20,100 result and identifies 2009 as the year of the sale.You use AI every day. articles.title: Exclusive Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 Space Marine Screenshots and Interview With Creative Director Jan Theysen
articles.summary: In this exclusive interview with director Jan Theysen, we go into detail on how the Space Marines actually work in Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4.
articles.body:
As development on Dawn of War 4 gathers pace like the Waaagh! of a planet-cracking Ork stampede, we’re getting a better sense of exactly how the real-time strategy Warhammer 40,000 game will play. King Art Games has already published numerous gameplay videos showing off competitive multiplayer, which will be an important part of the game, but how, exactly, will the Space Marines work?

You know the Space Marines, right? The poster boys of Games Workshop's Warhammer 40,000 tabletop are more often than not the stars of the show when it comes to video game adaptations. From the Ultramarines to the Space Wolves, the Space Marines have been leading the Warhammer 40,000 video game charge from day one. Indeed, the Dawn of War series' Blood Ravens, which were created by original developer Relic Entertainment, are now firmly entrenched within the Warhammer 40,000 canon as a legit chapter of Space Marines.

In Dawn of War 4 the Blood Ravens return, but this time they have help in the form of the Dark Angels and, briefly during the campaign, their primarch, Lion El'Jonson . In this exclusive interview with director Jan Theysen, we go into detail on how the Space Marines actually work in Dawn of War 4, explore some winning strategies, and find out what sets them apart from the Necrons, Orks, and the Adeptus Mechanics. We’ve also got a batch of exclusive screenshots showing off the Space Marines in all their glory, which you can view via the slideshow below.

IGN: How would you describe the Space Marine faction in terms of how it plays and how its different from the other factions at launch?

Jan Theysen: The Space Marines are definitely the most elite faction we have in the game. You control relatively few units that are pretty expensive, but also very good in what they're doing. You don't want to lose them. You want to protect your guys, you want to upgrade them. There are a lot of different equipments and abilities and so on. If you have your small, super well-equipped Space Marine Strike Force, you really want to care about it. So, especially in the early game, you really don't want to lose one of your units.

But the good news is that in the early game no other early game unit can defeat a Space Marine. They are the big boys. But also there are few. And so that is the challenge: wherever you are you are winning, but you are not everywhere.

Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 Space Marines Screenshots

IGN: What would you suggest as a good strategy for the Space Marines in multiplayer?

Jan Theysen: In Skirmish and in Multiplayer, it's very important in general to get out there quickly, to capture resource points and so on. But there's a little bit of a disadvantage for Space Marines, right? Because, compared to other factions, they can't quickly capture all the different points because you don't have that many units.

But whenever you see an enemy unit, you know you can probably kill it. So one good idea would be to go out there, maybe try to recapture enemy points pretty quickly because they can't get you off of the point easily again. Be aggressive and go after the enemy and only retreat if the enemy has like, two or maybe three units attacking you. You know that at some point you might think about retreating, or you might think about, just stand your ground, maybe auto heal your unit and wait until reinforcements appear, because that is also something you can do as Space Marines. You're relatively hard to kill. And so you can basically outlast even an overwhelming attack for some time, and wait or keep everybody occupied until the reinforcements arrive.

In general, the Space Marines can build anywhere on the map and they don't need a builder unit. They just call in the buildings from orbit. And so that is something you can keep in mind. You can maybe put some of your production buildings next to resource points, or almost build a little bit of a secondary base somewhere closer to the front line maybe, so that when you produce units they are already where you need them. And you can also produce units in reserve, which basically means that instead of producing the units and then having it on the battlefield already, you have the unit in orbit and can bring it down via Drop Pod or via Thunderhawk, which gives you a lot of flexibility. Because basically, if there is a surprise attack somewhere else, or if you spotted maybe a point that is not super well defended, you can just bring more units in and really quickly capture this point. These shock and awe tactics, so to speak, is really something that Space Marines excel at.

IGN: What are some of the little details you added to the Space Marines that players will notice?

Jan Theysen: A lot has to do with equipment and weapons. So when the Space Marines level up, you can give them better weapons, but not necessarily just a straight better weapon, but you can then start to specialise them. The Intercessors, for example, you can go for longer range or for more like an Auto Bolter, which fires faster. And you can push the units in a certain direction. And this is also true if you have something like a Dreadnought. Do you want a Dreadnought that's really strong against vehicles? Or do you want a Dreadnought that’s really strong against masses of infantry? And then you might pick a Gatling gun or you might pick a plasma gun. And so basically, Space Marines are super flexible.

To me they feel like in Dawn of War 1 where you had your units where you feel like, oh, these are my anti-infantry guys, and these are my whatever, and you build this little super specialised squad. Or maybe one or two units together. And then you have your hero killers or you have your vehicle destruction crew or something like that. And that is a lot of fun.

I think in general the Space Marines are probably one of the easier factions to play because you don't have that many units you have to control at any point. And since they're not that easy to kill, they forgive if you take a couple of seconds longer to realize that you're under attack. But on the other hand, if you then lose a couple of them, or if there's like a surprise attack from the enemy, it takes longer until you get back to full speed. Because not only do you have to buy a unit again if you lost a unit, but then you also have to upgrade them. And so you really want to make sure that you keep your units alive.

IGN: In terms of animation and design, how did you approach building the Space Marines so they don’t all run around looking like Buzz Lightyear?

Jan Theysen: I think we can all agree that Space Marines look badass, but this also comes with a lot of problems when you want to animate them, right? I mean, having these huge shoulders and having really restricted movement because of the armor and so on does not make your life easier. For the animators, it's figuring out how can we make sure that they feel right in terms of, they are very strong and they are very massive, but they are also very quick. Which is a little bit of a problem, right? Because if you have someone who's just very strong, but then very slow, you can easily communicate, okay, it's like a muscle mountain and usually slow but super strong. But you also want to make them quick, right? And so it's like, okay, if they're just stronger and quicker than everybody, then they are again kind of normal humans.

How can we communicate this strength? If a Space Marine fights an Ork, or they can also fight in our game a Guard in Multiplayer or in Skirmish, then you really see the difference. Then you really see, okay, how big a Space Marine is and how powerful a Space Marine is compared to other units.

And this was also one of the reasons why we actually start the game or the tutorial with the Guards. Because we wanted to set the baseline first. Like this is normal people, normal soldiers basically. And these are Space Marines, and this is how much better the Space Marines are. Because in the end, if everybody is like a super warrior then nobody is a super warrior.

IGN: What are the most powerful endgame Space Marine units?

Jan Theysen: In general, compared to other factions, the Space Marines do not have like this one super unit at the end. But they have a strong roster all the way through. They might even be a little bit focused on infantry because they have definitely a lot of different options there, including Terminators and Bladeguards and Eliminators, so very different kinds of infantry.

But then at some point you get the Dreadnoughts, which are already nice, but then you get the tanks. We have the Gladiator in two different versions: the Lancer and the Reaper. And then we have the Redemptor Dreadnought, which is the biggest tank in the game and also one of the biggest units in the game.

But compared to, let's say, an Imperial Knight, which is what the Ad Mech gets, they are not on the same level because they are still meant to be like a unit that you use in normal battles basically, or like in normal situations. So you might have two or three Reapers, you might have two or so Redemptor Dreadnoughts, and then you have your little tank strike force there. So it's not like this, okay, you have one of those, and this is like super special, right?

IGN: Which characters are available for the Space Marines and how do they work?

Jan Theysen: The Space Marines actually have the most characters and also the most playable characters. We have two Blood Ravens and two Dark Angel characters in the game. The Blood Ravens are Cyrus, who is basically a sniper / infiltrator who can hide, and he has a very long range weapon and a lot of stuff that revolves around hiding and scouting. Then we have Jonah Orion, who is a Librarian. He, of course, has a lot of different spells and stuff he can do to AOE attack.

Then we have for the Dark Angels, Astoran, who is a Captain in Terminator armor. He is the tankiest of the commanders we have in the game. You can equip him offensively, defensively, range, melee, so he's really, really flexible. But he is always super tanky. If you put him in a group with Bladeguards or other Terminators, that's definitely a brick that's hard to kill. And then lastly we have Ezrael, who is a Chaplain on Bike. And his main thing is, first of all, he's fast because he's an Outrider, but also, he can buff and motivate, so to speak, people around him. So he's very good at making others around him fight better. But he's also really a good character for just quick interventions. Because again, as a Space Marine, you have the problem that you can't be everywhere at once, right? So attach him to a unit of Outriders and have him as a fire brigade — something is burning, go figure it out. He's very, very useful for that.

IGN: Since the last time we spoke the game was pushed back to December. What are you now able to achieve that you wouldn't have been able to otherwise?

Jan Theysen: It's not like the one big thing we still wanted to do, right? It's more like there are a bunch of different things that we got from feedback from playtests and so on, where we felt like, oh yeah, that would be good to have it, it would be nice. Also, sometimes things we said, okay, we're probably not going to put it in the launch version, but then, that's definitely a we should do later on.

And then when we talked about, okay, do we want to launch in September or December? We basically said, okay, if we start in December or, you know, late November for the preorder guys, we could just put a lot more of these nice to have, should haves, and so on into the game and also, of course, just polish everything more in terms of performance and visuals.

And, as you know, this September is very busy. So a lot of things came together. We basically said, okay, this is probably the right decision because in the end, it's less than three months later, but we think the game is a lot better because of it.

Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 launches on PC on December 3, 2026.

articles.title: WWE Star John Cena Officially Rules Out a Return to the Ring: 'There Is No Chance That I'll Perform Again Physically'
articles.summary: John Cena has officially ruled out a return to physical performance in the WWE, having retired from professional wrestling in December.
articles.body:
John Cena has officially ruled out a return to physical performance in the WWE, having retired from professional wrestling in December.

The 17-time world champion hung up his jorts after an almost 25-year spell with the WWE following a submission defeat to Gunther in Washington, D.C. on December 13.

Since then there has been speculation from some fans that the Peacemaker actor may return to the ring, but in a new interview with the Today Show , he rubber stamped his retirement.

“I’m not going to perform again physically,” Cena declared. “There is no chance that I’ll perform again physically. And the WWE and I had a conversation about that, and we thought that at 49 it was the right time to step away. I put 23 years of physical service into the business.”

That’s that, then, for Cena’s career as a wrestler, but he’s not done with the WWE. He will return to the WWE in non-wrestling roles and as an ambassador, including the John Cena Classic in December. Cena said this live event will be based on the nostalgia for his WWE character, and the audience will decide the champion.

While Cena made a name for himself as a WWE star, he has also carved out a successful career as an actor. He has played DC anti-hero Peacemaker since 2021, including in James Gunn’s rebooted DC Universe, and there is an expectation that he will reprise the role either in an upcoming DCU movie or a potential Peacemaker Season 3. He’s currently promoting action comedy Matchbox: The Movie, which is based on the toy brand Matchbox by Mattel.

Who Is DC's Peacemaker? John Cena's The Suicide Squad Character Explained

Through it all is the question of whether a WWE retirement ever be considered genuine. Wrestlers have a habit of retiring and then returning to the ring, so while Cena has officially ruled out getting physical in the WWE again, I doubt anyone would be surprised if he came back for a match or two.

Still, his latest comments echo those he issued in June last year, before his final match. "There is no way," Cena told Good Morning America at the time. "There is absolutely... I don't want to speak in absolutes, because I don't want to close any opportunity, but I made a promise to the fans who've allowed me to be here for a quarter of a century. They allowed me to sit with you today. I wouldn't want to disrespect them like that. This is an event — when people attend, it's very exclusive."

The wrestler, who is considered one of the greatest of all time, also noted that he didn’t want to “ruin” the connection he’s built with fans throughout his career for the “selfish gain” of picking back up again after announcing his decision to step back from the sport.

articles.title: Warhammer Survivors Is Not Just a Vampire Survivors Clone, It Aims to Be a Celebration of the Best of Both Worlds | IGN Preview
articles.summary: Warhammer Survivors is shaping up to be another great adventure for fans of both Vampire Survivors and Warhammer, and I’m excited to see how the full game unfolds and adds to the fun I experienced in this short demo. It’s not doing anything groundbreaking, from what I can tell, but it has added meaningful additions that really honor the source material in a unique way that benefits gameplay. All I know is that all I want to do is jump back in for one… more… round… and that’s one of the highest compliments you can give any game.
articles.body:
There are few things more rewarding than the tide turning in your favor in Vampire Survivors. Starting as a weak soldier with one small attack and a fear of even the smallest foe, you soon become a literal weapon of mass destruction and turn a bullet hell of enemies into your own personal bullet heaven.

And you know what can make that feeling even better? Doing it with some trusty allies from the Warhammer 40,000 and Warhammer Age of Sigmar universes while using weapons pulled not just from the lore, but those inspired by how we engage with the tabletop game. Yes, we’re talking about the very dice we roll and paint we use to bring our miniatures to life. That, my friends, is Warhammer Survivors.

Warhammer Survivors Honors Warhammer 40,000 and Age of Sigmar’s Tabletop and Video Games

Warhammer Survivors is a standalone game developed and published by Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun’s Auroch Digital in partnership with Vampire Survivors’ Poncle, and it initially feels like returning home to the original title. However, you’ll quickly start to notice that it does enough things to stand tall on its own.

I spent a few hours with the demo you can download right now on PC via Steam and Xbox ahead of its November 10, 2026 release date, and I was able to check out both the Warhammer 40,000 side of the game and the Warhammer Age of Sigmar side. You read that right, there are two separate games included with their own unlocks, stages, achievements, and more.

We’ll start in Warhammer 40,000, as I first jumped into the armored shoes of Boltgun’s Malum Caedo, who starts with the Chainsword that is the weapon of choice for those within the Imperium of Man. However, in Vampire Survivors fashion, you quickly level up and gain access to new Weapons and Passives that make you increasingly more powerful.

As I teased before, you’ll find Boltguns and Lasguns and even Whirlwind Batteries that rain down missiles from above, but it’s the tabletop-inspired items that got me the most excited. If you are entrenched in the Warhammer universe, you’ll be very familiar with Nuln Oil, a very popular shade of paint. In Warhammer Survivors, this becomes a weapon that targets groups of enemies and damages them by splashing them with flammable oil.

Another fun weapon is the D6 Dice, which is inspired by the same dice that fuel its tabletop games. In Warhammer Survivors, these are represented by massive dice that come flying in off screen and will explode depending on what number they land on.

So not only are these giving a nod to the tabletop experience in a clever way, but they are giving it some serious gameplay ramifications, as enemies drenched in this Nuln Oil are even more susceptible to fire damage. This is all taken to greater heights when you learn there is an actual Hobby Table stage that has you playing on a workstation and that there’s a Paint Pot system that unlocks characters when certain combinations of colors are used. These little touches are so clever and don’t feel forced, they feel earned and welcome and add to the entire experience, just like the ally system.

In traditional Vampire Survivors, players are facing an endless horde of enemies by themselves and an array of weapons that fly in every direction away from and around them. In Warhammer Survivors, you get to bring some NPC friends along for the ride, and it’s awesome.

If you played Vampire Survivors’ Ode to Castlevania DLC, you’ll have a base understanding of how this works as they had a similar Familiars system, but you’ll be able to recruit other characters from the Warhammer universe to help you out on your run by choosing to select the weapons they would normally wield in the canon.

As an example, I may have started as Malum Caedo, but I was able to quickly add Trooper Bartosz Kozlowski to my crew (after I rescued him on the map from a circle of enemies and unlocked him as a playable character!) by choosing the Lasgun weapon. He followed me around and shot las bolts at the nearest enemy, and even more Astra Militarum troops joined as I leveled up the weapon. It honestly gave me the slightest link to Mass Effect 2, as I looked forward to recruiting all my allies for this epic war each run presented me with.

As for the runs themselves, they lasted anywhere from five minutes to over 20, and I enjoyed how there were always things to chase after. One of these objectives, which is represented by a question mark, is how you find characters like Trooper Bartosz Kozlowski or The Legend of Catachan. The latter character was the biggest challenge of the demo for me as he was surrounded by a circle of Warriors, who all used their Synapse Emitters to make any enemies within a close range of them even more powerful. Conquering that and unlocking The Legend of Catachan with a fun Super Smash Bros.-esque “Joins the battle!” screen was definitely a victory worth celebrating.

There are also a handful of objectives to accomplish that will unlock even more Weapons, Passives, and more, and it was a pleasant surprise when five or more of them unlocked after one run. These types of games just know how to give you that dopamine rush that keeps you coming back for more.

This was only the demo, so we’ll see how the full game plays out, but after rescuing the two characters and getting most of the objectives after a couple of hours, I did feel a bit of tedium start to set in. My biggest problem with Vampire Survivors was always feeling that the start could be very, very slow, as you are so weak and doing the same things over and over again, and I felt this a few times during my hands-on.

For example, to unlock The Legend of Catachan, I had to walk for nearly two minutes northeast to find him, and the grind started to show its ugly face after the fourth or fifth try as the movement is slow at first and you aren’t so powerful. There is supposed to be so much content in the full game - 40+ characters, 75+ weapons, 15+ stages, and countless objectives - so it will hopefully mitigate that somewhat, but it just reminded me of one of my few annoyances with Vampire Survivors.

Vermintide and Stormvermin and Clanrats!

For the last part of the story, we’re going to leave the Tyranids of Warhammer 40,000 and hop over to Warhammer Age of Sigmar and the ruthless Skaven. The two campaigns play the exact same, but it was fun jumping into a new universe and being able to unlock things all over again and take on a new foe. These enemies kept me on my toes, and the rat-like Vermintide may have been the most surprising. While I’m used to hordes and hordes of enemies descending on me every run, the Vermintide would, once in a while, swarm in horizontal lines on top of it all. This caused me to shift my strategy every time and actually gave the feeling of a bullet hell as I was weaving in and out of the rodent procession.

I also had my best run of the demo in Age of Sigmar as Neave Blacktalon, as this is when the stars aligned and the chests from stronger green-highlighted enemies were very much in my favor. These chests are all RNG-based, but when they shine on you, you can unlock upgrades for up to five Weapons or Passives, and it feels so great. What it also does, however, is get you closer to evolving said Weapons.

Neave Blacktalon starts with her Tempest Axes, and she can evolve them into Whirlwind Axes that are infused with lightning if you choose to unlock and level up the Sabaton Passive that makes your character faster. When you unlock one of these combinations, you feel as though you go Super Saiyan as your power level just dramatically increases.

This is also tied to one of my other frustrations with Warhammer Survivors in that it can be a bit tricky to really understand what goes with what without looking it up or getting lucky. For newcomers, this is a big hurdle because these are the key to longer, more successful runs. I’m all for trial and error and figuring things out, but this was a similar issue I had with Vampire Survivors. I didn’t feel like I got the game for a decent amount of runs, and I just wish the onboarding was a little better because I almost fell off before it clicked into a spectacular place.

However, once you do get it , you are in for just as much of a treat as Vampire Survivors. Does this do enough to convert those who may have not liked Vampire Survivors? Probably not. Is it shaping up to be a must-play for fans of Warhammer? Absolutely.

And everything I’ve discussed here is only scratching the surface. There are Extremis Bosses like the Norn Emissary that are the most challenging foes yet and turn this bullet heaven back into a bullet hell for a short time. There are Relics that can unlock different game modes, like one that does actually go faster and provide more EXP, and another that makes things even more daunting for the hardest of hardcore.

Warhammer Survivors is shaping up to be another great adventure for fans of both Vampire Survivors and Warhammer, and I’m excited to see how the full game unfolds and adds to the fun I experienced in this short demo. It’s not doing anything groundbreaking, from what I can tell, but it has added meaningful additions that really honor the source material in a unique way that benefits gameplay. All I know is that all I want to do is jump back in for one… more… round… and that’s one of the highest compliments you can give any game.

While you're here, check out these recent previews of other big upcoming games we've checked out recently!

articles.title: Starring Genden Phuntsok and Tom Hiddleston, Apple’s Tenzing Finally Places Mount Everest Pioneer Tenzing Norgay at the Center of His Own Ascent
articles.summary: Read our review of Apple TV’s Tenzing, a Mount Everest drama starring Genden Phuntsok and Tom Hiddleston that honors Sherpa Tenzing Norgay’s historic climb.
articles.body:
Tenzing premieres in select theaters October 9 and streams globally on Apple TV on October 16.

Tenzing is a moving drama about the real-life mountaineer Tenzing Norgay who, along with Edmund Hillary, were the first two people confirmed to have reached the summit of Mount Everest.

Historically, Hillary has received the lion’s share of attention for the epic deed, something that director Jennifer Peedom seeks to remedy by placing the Himalayan climber’s story at the forefront of her feature film debut. Tenzing largely succeeds at that although it must be noted that the film’s production notes state “creative license needed to be taken in certain areas to shape this complex history into a compelling cinematic narrative.”

Attempts to ascend Mount Everest have been the subject of many films and documentaries, some of which recount the tragedies and disasters that have befallen those who tried to reach the top. The mountain climbing movie genre itself presents a lot of tropes that are inescapable — treacherous terrain, vicious weather, near fatal plummets — as the perils of the grueling climb are obvious. And since the outcome here is a foregone conclusion, what makes Peedom’s film something special is its interwoven story about how Tenzing Norgay ended up there. As the film reveals, Tenzing had already faced many hardships and setbacks before he ever joined the 1953 British expedition.

The Luke Davies-scripted film depicts Tenzing’s boyhood as a yak herder growing up in the shadow of Mount Everest, which Tibetans call Chomolungma. His arduous youth eventually leads him from the Tibetan Plateau to Nepal (and later Darjeeling), where he’s left behind by his family. Wherever he goes, Tenzing finds himself an outsider and an underdog, constantly needing to prove himself and his value, whether it’s to the villagers for whom he toils in the Khumbu Valley or to the Brits assembling the climbing expedition.

Through it all, Tenzing endures thanks to his Buddhist faith and the love of his wife Dawa (the Adrian to his Rocky), whose untimely death breaks his heart but not his indomitable spirit. While the Brits and past European expeditions attempted to climb Everest for glory or national pride, Tenzing is on a spiritual quest to behold the face of Chomolungma, or what the Tibetans call the Mother Goddess of the World.

Drawing on her past work on the documentaries Sherpa, Mountain, and River, director Peedom has crafted a suitably majestic-looking film but wisely makes sure to keep it about people and not just breathtaking vistas. The film benefits from its exploration of the cultural differences between the Brits and the Sherpas (a distinct ethnic culture from the people Tenzing hails from, and a source of tension and mistrust by some of the Sherpas he’s hired). This also helps forge the bond between Tenzing and Hillary, himself an outsider on the Expedition as the Brits enjoy pointing out that he’s a Kiwi. The two men recognize their similarities rather than just their differences, establishing a deep trust that proves vital to their success on the mountain.

Tenzing is portrayed by three different actors: Samdrup Dorje Lama as a boy, Tenzin Dalha as a young man, and Genden Phuntsok as the older Tenzing. All three actors are great, but this is Phuntsok’s show. He imbues Tenzing with charm and pluck, and has fun chemistry with Tom Hiddleston’s Hillary (the Loki actor never attempts to try to one-up Phuntsok, fully understanding that he’s a supporting player here). Phuntsok and Hiddleston make for an endearing pair and they keep the viewer invested in their journey even when you know they won’t perish.

Willem Dafoe and Caitríona Balfe have supporting roles, with Dafoe’s expedition leader Col. John Hunt as the stuffy imperial who may not be as much of a jerk as first expected. Balfe is always a glowing presence in any project, but there is precious little she has to do here as Jill Henderson, the secretary of the Himalayan Club who sees something special in Tenzing. Faring somewhat better (albeit in a fairly two-dimensional role) is Thinley Lhamo as Dawa, whose warmth and humor make it easy to believe why Tenzing loved her so much.

While I’m a sucker for a good underdog movie, I concede that someone else might view Tenzing the movie as too slight or sentimental, that perhaps the story has Tenzing overcome his challenges too quickly or easily. All I can say I simply enjoyed being in Tenzing’s company and appreciated the light and hope the film emits in these dark times.

articles.title: GameStop and Third-Party Resellers Raise Used PS5 Pro Price to $1,400 — a $500 Markup on Sony's RRP
articles.summary: GameStop and third-party resellers have raised the price of used PS5 Pros to as little as $1,400, a $500 markup on Sony's suggested retail price.
articles.body:
GameStop and third-party resellers have raised the price of used PS5 Pro consoles to as much as $1,400 — a $500 markup on Sony's suggested retail price.

Last night, rumors began flying around that GameStop would be jacking up the price on pre-owned PS5 Pros to $1,399 for an all-digital PS5 Pro. That was confirmed this morning when the company's website was updated with this price point. Third-party resellers who move products through Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart have also changed their prices to similar amounts. The price hike appears to be a result of the overwhelming demand for Sony's premium console, which had a price increase earlier this year that raised the price from $750 to $900.

Demand is expected to be high for the console due to the release of GTA 6, which will most likely take advantage of the console's extra power. However, Sony is unable to meet that demand due to ongoing component shortages, which has allowed the pre-owned market to ask for more money than they normally would.

articles.title: Star Wars Actor Says He Was Told to Cut Off His Dreadlocks as They'd Be Too 'Realistic,' Despite The Franchise Being About 'Giant Slugs and Swords Made of Light'
articles.summary: Star Wars actor Jordan Stephens says he declined to return in hit Disney+ series Andor after being told to cut off his dreadlocks — to ensure his appearance looked "realistic."
articles.body:
Star Wars actor Jordan Stephens says he declined to return in hit Disney+ series Andor after being told to cut off his dreadlocks to ensure his appearance looked "realistic."

Stephens, better known as half of U.K. rap duo Rizzle Kicks, originally appeared as Rebel Alliance soldier Corporal Tonc in Star Wars: Rogue One . While Tonc died in the movie, he — and many other actors — were invited back for the subsequent prequel series Andor in order to better flesh out his role.

Unfortunately for Stephens, his return came with a caveat: that he cut off his dreadlocks he had been growing for seven years in order to film "for a day." Speaking to Zeteo , Stephens said he had even argued his case to point out that he had been wearing a helmet throughout his Rogue One appearance, which would have hidden his locks again in Andor. Alas, he was told this still would not be good enough — and Stephens walked away.

Rogue One: 17 Cool Star Wars Details Revealed by the Writers

"In Rogue One, I'm wearing a helmet the whole time. So I was like, yeah I've got locks but who cares, just put me in a helmet [again]," he began.

"'Well, we're going to shoot scenes of the army training'," he claimed he was then told in response by an unknown person connected to the series' production. "'We're going to be training so we're going to need you in traditional army attire, including your hair. And if you have locks, I don't think it'd be realistic'."

To this, Stephens says he reacted incredulously, pointing out that Star Wars was far from a realistic franchise. The rapper also admitted that the offer came with "f*** all" money for his appearance.

"I was like, you're talking about an intergalactic space war with giant slugs and swords made of light, and you're worried about a soldier having dreadlocks?" he concluded. "On principal... the cognitive dissonance was too difficult to handle. The idea that someone would watch and say 'oh, well he's got dreadlocks so it's obviously not real'... what is going on? It's absolutely insane."

Ranking the Star Wars Disney+ Live-Action TV Shows

The hair-cutting requirement for Stephens to return meant that the muscian and actor ultimately missed out on appearing in one of the best Star Wars projects in recent years — if not all time. Andor is frequently praised by fans as being Disney's best production in the franchise, and is absolutely worth your time if you have not yet watched it to date.

Oh, and the idea that Star Wars characters can't have dreadlocks? This is clearly ridiculous, and undermined by the appearance of Jedi Master Quinlan Vos throughout the Clone Wars series — who has dreadlocks himself.

articles.title: 'If You Can't Own It, What Are You Buying?' – Former PlayStation Boss Questions Sony's Decision to Kill Discs
articles.summary: Ever since Sony decided to kill off PlayStation discs starting in 2028, the backlash has been pronounced to say the least. And, now, it looks like former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden is also questioning Sony's decision.
articles.body:
Ever since Sony decided to kill off PlayStation discs starting in 2028, the backlash has been pronounced to say the least. And, now, it looks like former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden is also questioning Sony's decision.

Last week, Layden was interviewed in an episode of The Expansion Pass podcast , where he was asked about his take on Sony's decision to kill discs. And while he makes it clear that he wasn't in the room for the decision, he prefaces his take by saying "gamers are... yeah, we like the digital download. People said, 'Oh, downloading a game is easier than going to the store!' No, no, downloading a game is easier than going across my living room to put a disc in the machine. I don't even have to do that."

But while digital downloads have always been a win for convenience, Layden said he still believes the decision to kill off discs completely is misguided.

"But I do think, particularly in the gaming realm, maybe 80% of the people download and 20% don't, whatever that breakdown might be, but that's a super important 20%," he said. "I mean, that is largely the most faithful of the faithful, that is, many times, the people who buy two copies of every game, one never gets out of the shrink wrap, and you play the other one."

There are definitely people out there who collect unopened games to put on their shelves, but the bigger issue about this move is the question of ownership. Now, over on PC, we've had to live with this reality for years, thanks to the proliferation of Steam and digital games, but even then, there's at least GOG, which will let you download a game without DRM a lot of the time that you can just archive on your own disc.

But PlayStation will likely never get that option, so the question about ownership is huge, and something that Layden catches onto here.

"It changes the conversation from 'do you own a game, or do you have access to a digital asset?" Layden concluded. "If you can't sell a thing, it means you don't own a thing. If you don't own it, then what are you buying? If you're buying access that doesn't quite sound as sexy, to be honest."

Layden does hit the core of the issue here, and while Sony would likely argue that you were still buying access to a digital access when you were buying the disc, the loss of the tangible item really makes that illusion disappear. From there, it's easy to see why people look at Sony pulling access to movies and imagine that the same is going to happen for their games.

For his part, Layden makes that same connection, noting that, "As people tend to do, in their mind, they'll game out the worst case scenario. And that's a whole lot of brand hit and reputation bite." It certainly was a huge hit to Sony's reputation . Only time will tell, now, whether or not the money Sony saves by not producing discs will be worth the ill will it generated when it killed discs.

Sony does seem intent on making unpopular moves. Earlier this month it filed a couple of patents that would use AI to create vibe-coded patches to fix your PS5, and another that would put an NFC card reader in your controller .

articles.title: Michael Bay in Talks to Direct Next Transformers Film, Steven Spielberg Returning as Key Creative Producer
articles.summary: Michael Bay is reportedly in early conversations to direct the next Transformers movie following a successful meeting with Steven Spielberg, who is returning to produce the new installment.
articles.body:
Michael Bay is reportedly in early conversations to direct the next Transformers movie following a successful meeting with Steven Spielberg, who is returning to produce the new installment.

Deadline reports that Spielberg has been appointed to "focus on all creative aspects" as a producer of the next live-action Transformers film, a role that he held on the first two Bay-directed films. As a result, Spielberg will spearhead the creative direction of the next film with the help of long-time producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura. Paramount has been courting Spielberg for a year to help lead the next Transformers film, and he finally agreed to do so after reading a script from Jason Fuchs, a writer who has contributed to the It films and Wonder Woman. Plot details are under wraps, but it's expected to be set in the modern day.

Paramount also courted Michael Bay for the last year, and he entered conversations to come aboard as director last week after reading the script and meeting with Spielberg. As of right now, nothing is locked in place with Bay, but it seems like something Paramount is eager to make happen.

Michael Bay spent a decade directing Transformers films, helming the franchise's first five live-action movies. He eventually walked away, and Paramount produced two more, including a Bumblebee prequel and Transformers: Rise of the Beasts. Those two films performed reasonably well, but fell far below the billion-dollar receipts that Bay had raked in some of his other outings.

Bay's films were box office behemoths, but were often criticized for taking a more violent approach to the robots in disguise. The films also had rocky plots and questionable humor, but some of them have been reappraised in recent years for their impressive CG, stylish visuals, and epic action sequences. Actor Robert Pattinson even called Bay's first Transformers the "definitive movie of the 2000s."

Spielberg had also advised Bay to stop making Transformers films after his third movie, but the studio asked him to make more. The director noted that he regrets not listening to Spielberg , but it seems both have had a change of heart.

Whether Bay will be served with a better script that can pair with his chaotic style remains to be seen, but it could be an epic return. Unfortunately, whatever happens with the next film, Optimus Prime actor Peter Cullen will not return. The actor passed away earlier this year , meaning the studio will have to recast or put Optimus on the bench in the next installment.

The tan and white tones would go with just about any outfit, and you still get casual nods to the flying bison’s striped fur. You also get tons of cozy fur lining.

This one swaps the bold orange back for the softened tan, but adds in some soft blue accents. Almost all of the shoe designs feature Aang’s airbending arrow in some form, but this one makes it most obvious.

All of the new collection comes in limited edition ATLA-themed packaging, which, if you’re a fan of collecting random boxes, is honestly pretty cool in and of itself.

articles.title: A Scoundrel in the New World: Blacksad's Juanjo Guarnido Tackles the Legend of El Dorado
articles.summary: We've got an exclusive look at A Scoundrel in the New World, the latest stunning graphic novel from Blacksad artist Juanjo Guarnido.
articles.body:
Anytime Blacksad artist Juanjo Guarnido announces a new project, we're going to take notice. That's what makes the new graphic novel A Scoundrel in the New World so exciting. This new satirical adventure graphic novel explores the legendary Treasure of El Dorado as only Guarnido could render it.

With the Kickstarter campaign for A Scoundrel in the New World live now, IGN can exclusively debut a new preview of the book. Check it out in the slideshow gallery below:

A Scoundrel in the New World Preview Gallery

A Scoundrel in the New World is written by Alain Ayroles (Garulfo) and illustrated by Guarnido. The book acts as a sequel to Francisco de Quevedo’s 1626 novel The Life of the Swindler named Don Pablos. It's published in a partnership between Oni Press and Magnetic Press. Here's the official summary of the project:

Inspired by Francisco de Quevedo classic 1626 satirical novel Historia de la vida del Buscón, llamado don Pablos (The Life of the Swindler named Don Pablos), A SCOUNDREL IN THE NEW WORLD follows Don Pablos of Segovia, a charming conman and inveterate liar who leaves behind the treacherous streets of Spain in search of fortune in the New World. After a life of misadventure, Don Pablos finds himself in prison, recounting his experiences to greedy inquisitors as the ultimate unreliable narrator. From the opulent, gilded halls of the colonial elite to the untamed jungles of the young Americas, Pablos weaves a web of complex schemes to climb the social ladder. However, as the lines between his tall tales and reality begin to blur, Pablos discovers that in the colonies, the most dangerous predator isn’t the wilderness: it’s human ambition.

“A Scoundrel in the New World may be Juanjo Guarnido’s most ambitious work to date, even compared to his work as the co-creator and artist of the world-famous Blacksad series,” said Magnetic Press’ Director of Publishing, Mike Kennedy, in a statement. “Every panel is a painting, filled with immaculate historical detail, expressive characters, and cinematic lighting that really brings the period to life with vibrant intensity. Alain Ayroles’ script is a brilliant homage to the Golden Age of Spanish literature, a witty and somewhat cynical tale employing a shifting ‘Rashomon-style’ perspective that keeps the reader questioning the protagonist’s credibility until the final page. This book combines the cynical historical wit of Blackadder with the sprawling adventure of El Dorado.”

articles.title: Sony Patent Would Let an AI Model Train NPCs Based on Your Player Data
articles.summary: If one thing's been abundantly clear over the last year is that Sony and Microsoft are both chomping at the bit to work AI features into the next generation of consoles. And, now Sony has filed another patent that would use AI to train NPCs based on data generated by you, the player.
articles.body:
If one thing's been abundantly clear over the last year, it's that Sony and Microsoft are both champing at the bit to work AI features into the next generation of consoles. And now, Sony has filed another patent that would use AI to train NPCs based on data generated by you, the player.

This new patent, called "AI-adapted non-player character for video game system," describes a process of taking data generated from playing a game and then using it to modify NPCs in order to make them more lifelike.

But unlike Nvidia's ACE program , which uses a large language model to essentially script NPC dialogue, Sony's proposed system could change everything about an NPC, from its design to its behavior in, say, a boss fight. Sony asserts that this is necessary to create more lifelike games, without bloating development time and budgets even more than they already are.

The patent says that "developing such believable NPCs is challenging due to limitations of modern game development and often relies extensive scripting and programming. Additionally, NPC development often relies on sophisticated systems and extensive resources to track, animate, and evolve NPC behaviors. In a typical development environment, NPC management often utilizes costly and efficient rendering engines, simulation engines, and scalable systems capable of supporting increasingly detailed virtual environments and lifelike NPC interactions."

The solution, according to this patent, is to use AI to do most of this work. It continues, "The techniques described herein overcome the foregoing challenges and others by providing an artificial intelligence (AI)-adapted NPC. By using the techniques described herein, video game systems can be improved." Using AI to shortcut development time is nothing new, but that's not the whole reason that Sony patented this technology. It seems to think the player data will make NPCs even better than before."

Sony continues: "Additionally, by using the techniques described herein, lifelike NPCs that behave based on behaviors exhibited by video game players and/or responsive to behaviors exhibited by video game players can be seamlessly integrated into video game systems and video game content thereby improving video game systems without the extensive scripting and hardware resources."

inZOI Gameplay Screenshots (Early Access)

Just like any of the other patents that Sony has been spitting out at a rapid clip, there's no guarantee this system would actually make its way to a PlayStation 5 (or more likely PlayStation 6) near you. However, the game industry has been experimenting with ways to use AI to train NPCs for years now. Just last year, Inzoi used LLMs, along with player input to shape how NPCs would interact with the player and each other.

It's only a matter of time, then, before AI is used to train different parts of NPC behavior with your data. I could see a world where the bosses in a game like Elden Ring evolve to counter your playstyle, or an enemy in a horror game stalking you more effectively because it 'knows' how you react to different stimuli.

However, there would be questions about security. As cool as having smarter NPCs would be, if these models are processed in the cloud, there would be a risk of your data leaking out onto the internet. And while it doesn't seem like advertisers would want know how you react to a giant monster swinging an axe at you, it probably will end up being used for 'enhanced marketing,' too.

This is hardly the first of Sony's strange new patents. Just a couple of weeks ago, the company patented a system where AI would detect problems with your console and deliver vibe-coded patches . It also patented a controller with an NFC card reader that would bring tap-to-pay to your PlayStation. The next generation of consoles is shaping up to be a strange one, to say the least.

articles.body:
Doctor Who may be on hiatus, but the BBC has just unveiled a new spinoff series for younger viewers: Doctor Who: TARDIS Crew.

This animated series will feature a "young" version of the Doctor who is shown in official artwork to sport blue spiky hair. Clearly, this is not an incarnation of the Time Lord we have met previously — unless William Hartnell was really into hair dye in his youth.

Today's reveal for the series includes a confirmation of the production company behind the show, the London-based Alphablocks and Numberblocks creator Blue Zoo Animation Studio, and a projected launch in late 2027 or early 2028 — around a year before the BBC is aiming to bring the main Doctor Who back to U.K. TV screens.

"Created for CBeebies viewers, the series follows the Doctor, a young Time Lord, and his friends Hannah, Beastie and Toast-IE as they embark on extraordinary adventures through time and space," reads a blurb for the show. "Travelling aboard the iconic TARDIS, they encounter incredible creatures, discover amazing new worlds and come face-to-face with legendary Doctor Who foes, including the Daleks."

The 25 Most Essential Doctor Who Episodes

While this isn't the first we've heard of a new Doctor Who spinoff for younger viewers, this is the first time we've seen anything of its characters or aesthetic. The BBC has now also commissioned 52 episodes, each 11 minutes in length, with "preschool-friendly stories."

Artwork for the series shows the young Doctor wielding his trusty sonic screwdriver, his pink-hatted companion Hannah holding a cute pink alien pet, and a robot toaster sidekick (how very Red Dwarf!). The Daleks are present too, of course, albeit sporting a rather cutesy redesign. One of them even has a wooden spoon as an appendage, which I enjoy.

Putting on my nerd hat for a moment, it's worth considering when this series might be set in Doctor Who canon (if indeed it is to be considered canon). The description of the Doctor as young suggests we could be seeing a pre-Hartnell incarnation of the Time Lord — one of the many forgotten variants the franchise now seems happy to explore following its controversial Timeless Child revelation that the 16 main Doctors to date are just the latest in a much longer lineage.

Not setting this new spinoff in the era of any other Doctor allows the series freedom to explore the Whoniverse without relying on certain actors or fitting into specific timelines. Still, as a time-travel show, we'd be shocked if David Tennant didn't put in an appearance at some point.

One person who won't be involved in Doctor Who: TARDIS Crew is the franchise's former showrunner Russell T Davies, who this week discussed his exit and said he wasn't bothered about leaving his Billie Piper cliffhanger unresolved .

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: Forza Horizon 6's Community Is Fed Up With Playground Games, and the Studio Has Finally Responded
articles.summary: Forza Horizon 6 developer Playground Games has finally addressed its player community after months of constructive feedback about the game has been met with nothing but radio silence from the renowned British studio.
articles.body:
Forza Horizon 6 developer Playground Games has finally addressed its player community after months of constructive feedback about the game has been met with nothing but radio silence from the renowned British studio.

"Hey Horizon Community," the post on the studio's social channels begins, "We're reading all your comments about Forza Horizon 6, and we realize that we haven't been talking with you as much as we could be. While we continue to deliver regular content and fixes into the game, we want you to know we hear your feedback about our post-launch updates and we're looking into future changes to both in-game content and the ways we communicate with you. Stay tuned!"

Forza Horizon 6 got rave reviews upon its release – including a 10 out of 10 from IGN – but Playground's lack of communication with its players has frustrated the community. As detailed in videos from Forza Horizon content creators STEVIO2175 , AR12Gaming , HokiHoshi , and Ericship 111 , players are upset at the live service game's complete absence of communication from Playground as well as some features from previous Forza games that are missing from the newest Horizon.

"It just feels like the community engagement between the developers and us is just nonexistent," STEVIO2175 said in his excellent and thorough 19-minute video on the subject from late August. Players are feeling like they have to spend their time in the Horizon Festival playlists in order to get access to the new cars – many of which are recycled from previous Horizon games – rather than play in whatever modes and ways they want.

Playground's Forza Monthly show that directly interfaces with the community has also been absent, leading some in the Forza space to wonder if it's a side effect of new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's big " reset " and subsequent layoffs. The lack of in-game voice chat in Horizon 6 is also on the community's list of constructive criticisms – a particularly curious omission from FH6 given that the previous entry in the Forza series, 2023's Forza Motorsport, has voice chat to this day. "Voice chat alone could make FH6 Japan ten times better," STEVIO2175 said. "But the thing that bothers me most at the end of the day," he added, "is that the devs have not responded at all. No communication, no public responses, nothing."

More to the point, STEVIO2175 said he believes that most players don't feel like this game has replayability past single player. "Until the socialization and community features get added, if they ever do, player interest is going to continue to drop," STEVIO2175 said. "And I hope they figure this all out before PS5 hopefully still gets this game."

On that note, Microsoft and Playground still have not announced a release date for the PlayStation 5 version of Forza Horizon 6 despite it being October now and the last the companies said , it'd ship on PS5 this year. That looks increasingly unlikely by the day, but perhaps it's for the best if Playground needs to iron out all of its communication and content roadmap criticisms from the community before launching on another platform.

A second team at Playground is also in the stretch run of development on the Fable reboot, which is due to be released on Xbox, PC, and PS5 on February 23, 2027. It's fair to wonder if Fable has been pulling resources away from Forza Horizon 6 as the former team makes its final sprint to the finish line. We finally got to play Fable at Gamescom in August and were quite pleased by the combat .

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title: Nolan North Is Staying in Shape Just in Case Sony Calls About Uncharted 5
articles.summary: Uncharted star Nolan North is keen to return for Uncharted 5, amid reports that a fresh entry in the franchise is in production.
articles.body:
Uncharted star Nolan North is keen to return for Uncharted 5, amid reports that a fresh entry in the franchise is in production .

While Sony is yet to officially announce any new Uncharted project, Naughty Dog has confirmed it has multiple games in the works right now. Aside from the upcoming Intergalactic: Heretic Prophet, it is believed that Uncharted: The Lost Legacy director Shaun Escayg is leading a team building a fresh entry in the company's beloved adventure series.

North, who portrays Uncharted hero Nathan Drake, has now said he would happily return to the role if asked — and has even tried to stay in shape for whenever the call comes. Perhaps unsurprisingly, North is also bullish on Uncharted 5's likelihood of success if it is indeed released — while also acknowledging that Naughty Dog needed to avoid launching something as unpopular as the fourth Indiana Jones movie, Kingdom of the Crystal Skull.

Uncharted Games in (Chronological) Order

"I think it would be one of the biggest games ever if they decided to do it," North said, speaking during the Gamergy show in Puerto Rico (thanks, DomTheBomb / VGC ). "It just depends if Sony wants to make money.

"I haven't heard anything, but you know, it is a business and my God, can you imagine if they if they did? I mean, it would be the biggest announcement in gaming. And I don’t think that’s hyperbole, I think that's true. I think that would be... to bring back a storied franchise like that? You just don't want to make a Kingdom of the Crystal Skull."

While Intergalactic is believed to be the next project to launch from Naughty Dog, the studio still has a legion of fans keen for new entries in its other franchises: The Last of Us and Uncharted. It's now been a decade since Uncharted 4 released and put a nice bow on Nathan Drake's adventures, but this gap in time also opens up the possibility of a fresh adventure that featured his daughter, Cassie.

"You know, I try to stay in shape, just in case," Nolan concluded. "It was 10 years of work with good friends, good people, a great developer. I can't see a scenario that I would say no."

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social
