articles.title: Battlefield 6 Resurrects the Corpse of Dead Space With The Marker Tease
articles.summary: The corpse of Dead Space is being reinimated for Battlefield 6, with the latest trailer for Season 5 seemingly teasing a crossover.
articles.body:
The corpse of Dead Space is being reinimated for Battlefield 6 , with the latest trailer for Season 5 seemingly teasing a crossover.

Battlefield 6’s new trailer shows off a new Las Vegas map that looks like a lot of fun, as choppers and machine guns tear up casinos and skyscrapers along The Strip. But then the music fades out, ominous sounds creep in, and it cuts to a bloom-filled scene where two Dead Space engineers stare up at The Marker, the survival horror series’ alien artifact that drills into your brain.

Earlier this year, series writer Chuck Beaver claimed sales were too low for EA to greenlight a Dead Space 4 . Series co-creator and developer of The Callisto Protocol, Glen Schofield, also retired from the industry this year after his spiritual successor failed to light up the industry.

Battlefield 6 players on Reddit already spotted potential Dead Space skins, which were rumored to launch in the Halloween update this October, so that’s probably what you can expect. Developers at Dice have previously gone on the record to say Battlefield 6 won’t feature goofy, immersion breaking skins . That’s done now, if these rumors are true.

EA recently added a Dead Space skin to Skate and charged $40 for it so there's precedent for skins in the universe. Players weren’t happy with the skin itself or the cost, so it’ll be interesting to see if EA aims for more realistic pricing for the next crossover. Battlefield 6 previously did a crossover event with Top Gun , but that makes sense in a game featuring fighter jets.

Battlefield 6’s fifth Season features three new maps, including Vegas Strip and Area 51, six new weapons and two new vehicles. You can jump into Vegas on October 13.

Dead Space Graphic Comparison - Remake vs Original

As for Dead Space, talking on the FRVR Podcast , Beaver said that to recoup the costs of the franchise's high production values, any new game would need to sell over 10 million copies — a tall order for even a breakout horror game.

“Any of the Resident Evils are selling around seven million [copies], that’s a pretty good number," Beaver said. "But, you know, companies now are looking for the next Fortnite . They need something that is a perennial moneymaker… something like a single-player package game with no live-service offering that’s like it’s just a dinosaur fossil of a business model."

The Dead Space remake, developed by EA-owned Motive Studio and released in 2023, was well-received but appears to have not done enough business to convince the powers that be at the mega publisher to invest in a follow-up. IGN's Dead Space remake review returned a 9/10. We said: "Dead Space is a superb remake and undoubtedly the definitive way to experience one of the best survival horror shooters that Capcom never made."

“Horror games have a bit of a ceiling, you know, and I think the number back in [former EA VP] Frank Gibeau’s day was 5 million units to keep going on Dead Space," Beaver continued. "I think the number is like 15 million units now, given the cost of things," he added, before joking that it was "a sadness in capitalism for all of us to suffer, until AI makes it apparently easy for you and I just type 'make Dead Space 4.'"

In October last year, Schofield told IGN he hoped to bring the franchise back to life , despite EA's lack of interest. “I went to [EA] recently and they're like, 'No, we're not interested anymore,'” he said. “I said, 'I can get back the leadership team. I need the models from EA Motive and I can save you 30 to 40 million dollars on the idea that I have.' And, they're like, 'No.'"

“I have quite a few ideas that I'm ready to go with and one of them is Dead Space 4,” Schofield continued. “The fact that EA just got bought, I think there’s an opportunity. I’m already making calls.”

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: Amazon Restocks Rare Pokémon TCG Sets for Prime Day

articles.body:
Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days sale is now fully underway, and there are more than enough standout offers to get your teeth stuck into over the next couple of days. Yes, this is a remarkably short sale by Amazon's recent standards, lasting just 48 hours through October 6-7.

There are a few new Pokémon TCG items that have been restocked as part of the sale, including 30th anniversary First Partner Collections, Surging Sparks, and Perfect Order boosters, and loads more.

The selection isn't quite as spectacular as we've seen in previous restocks, such as during Pokémon Day or Labor Day, but it's still not bad at all. Let's take a look at what's up for grabs.

Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolutions - Perfect Order 3 Pack Blister (Chikorita)

For now, let's start with the biggest and best finds from this Labor Day restock. Pokémon TCG's First Partner Illustration Collection Series 3 is part of Pokémon's 30th anniversary celebrations. This release marks the final chapter in the First Partner Illustration TCG Collection.

Series 1 took us back to the classic roots with Kanto (Gen 1), Sinnoh (Gen 4), and Alola (Gen 7). Series 2 took us back to the Johto (Gen 2), Unova (Gen 5), and Galar (Gen 8) regions. Series 3 officially rounds out the whole collection, bringing us the beloved first partner Pokémon from the Hoenn, Kalos, and Paldea regions.

Listed median prices for these is $34 at TCGplayer , which is bang on what Amazon is listing it for as well. Average market price is around $30-$35 (not including delivery), so Amazon is probably your best bet for these, especially if you're picking up two or three, and even more so if you're an Amazon Prime member with free speedy delivery.

Same as the other two series, inside each box, you'll score:

1 Pokémon TCG Pack: Contains 3 of 9 illustration rare-style promo cards featuring the First Partner Pokémon from Gen 3 (Treecko, Torchic, Mudkip), Gen 6 (Chespin, Fennekin, Froakie), and Gen 9 (Sprigatito, Fuecoco, and Quaxly).

2 Pokémon TCG Booster Packs (pulled from Pitch Black and Chaos Rising).

1 Exclusive Sticker Sheet featuring the Collection’s starter crew.

Amazon currently has the 30th Celebration ETB listed for just $159.99 , considerable up from the $89.99 price we spotted previously. A bit annoying for those who missed out on the better deal, but Amazon having stock and still allowing invites is better than absolutely nothing.

The timing here is worth paying attention to. When we first spotted Amazon taking invite requests at below $90, the 30th Celebration set hadn't yet fully hit the market. Now that the 30th Anniversary collection is officially out, we're seeing just how difficult some of its products can be to find at a reasonable price .

The bigger problem is that requesting an invite doesn't mean Amazon will actually offer you the ETB , even if you are willing to pay the $160. The retailer previously introduced invite requests for this product in the US, an unusual move given that Amazon's US Pokémon TCG listings have traditionally been priced much closer to prevailing market prices.

Amazon also has the rare Surging Sparks boosters back in stock at what is an eye watering $17.59 per booster pack. Yeesh. TCGplayer is running these for below $10 still, so you may be better off buying from a third-party reseller in all honestly. But, the option is there at Amazon, along with all the other products in the restock, if you so desire.

But is it worth it? Only you can be the judge of that. The "market price" is often dictated by what the majority of people are willing to pay, but only you can decide if this if truely worth your money.

No matter how unfortunate it is, and how hard it is to find Pokémon TCG at MSRP , market value is often the price you have to pay now, even from big retailers like Amazon, as I mentioned.

To see all the recently restocked items at Amazon, be sure to check out our custom search tracker to ensure you're buying sealed boosters that are only "sold and shipped" directly from Amazon itself.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

articles.title: The Game of Thrones Complete Series 4K Box Set Drops Under $100 for the First Time Ever
articles.body:
George R.R. Martin's A Song of Ice of Fire is deep into spin-off TV territory these days, but it was the original Game of Thrones series that started it all. If you're hoping to pick up all eight seasons for your collection, the 4K box set has dropped to its lowest price of all time for Prime Big Deal Days .

This Game of Thrones collection was released back in March 2026, and this is the first time the price has dropped under $100. The box set includes every episode as well as 15 hours of added bonus features.

Games of Thrones: The Complete Collection (4K Ultra HD)

While it's true that you can stream Game of Thrones with an HBO Max subscription, you'll need to have the most expensive tier to actually get it in 4K . So if you love the series and want to add it in your collection for a re-watch, the 4K box set is a great way to do just that.

Streaming in 4K is a modern marvel, but it still doesn't hold a candle to the kind of picture you can get from physical discs . The 4K Blu-ray discs are undoubtedly the best way to experience the series in high-definition. All you need is a decent 4K Blu-ray player and you'll be in for a visual treat.

I'll be the first to admit that the final season of Game of Thrones kind of put me off the series for a while. It wasn't the ending I really wanted, and that can partially be blamed on George R.R. Martin having not finished The Winds of Winter .

That being said, I did recently rewatch the entire series again and fell in love with it all over again. That final season doesn't make the earlier seasons any less wonderful, and I found myself spotting things I'd never seen all those years ago. With House of the Dragon and A Knight of the Kingdom breathing new life into the series, I think it's absolutely worth going back and watching all of the episodes again. There's a reason this is one of the most popular shows of all time, after all.

articles.title: Save 50% Off the Massive 98" TCL QM8L 4K TV With Super Quantum Dot Technology During Prime Day
articles.summary: At this size, it's a better option than even OLED.
articles.body:
One of the best super big screen TVs drops to its lowest price ever for Prime Day . Amazon is currently offering the massive 98" TCL QM8L 4K TV for $2,998.99 with free shipping. If you're an Amazon Prime cardmember, then you also get an extra 10% cashback instead of the typical 5%. This TV normally costs $6,000. If you're looking for a TV that's near 100" in size, then I would recommend this TV over any other brand or model. Yes, even over OLED.

Save 50% ($3,000) Off the New 2026 98" TCL QM8L SQD 4K TV

Extra 10% cashback for Amazon Prime members

98" TCL QM8L 4K SQD Mini-LED Google TV (2026)

TCL's SQD mini LED tech seems like the real deal

The new 2026 QM8L TV features TCL's highly-touted SQD technology. SQD - which stands for Super Quantum Dot - is a more refined version of QLED tech. Quantum dot panels have a layer of microscopic crystals measuring a few nanometers in size that are able to separate light into precise colors. SQD tech uses even smaller crystals - as small as a single nanometer in width. This allows SQD panels to pack in even more dimming zones, usually numbering in the thousands, which in turn produces a brighter image with higher contrast and richer colors. The 98" model in particular boasts up to 6,000nits of peak brightness and over 4,000 local dimming zones.

Combined with TCL's new Halo Control System, the QM8L eliminates the halo effect you get with other LED LCD TVs when white and black elements are placed next to each other. This is one way you can distinguish OLED TVs (which don't exhibit the halo effect) to LED LCD TVs. TCL's SQD TV levels the playing field in that respect. The QM8L is also a great option for console gaming. The panel boasts a native 144Hz refresh rate and four total HDMI 2.1 ports.

I'd pick the 98" QM8L over the 97" LG G6 OLED

On the OLED front, the closest comparison to the 98" TCL QM8L would be the LG G6 Gallery series TV , which is available in a 97" screen size. Let's ignore the fact that the TV costs $20,000 at most retailers and that OLED burn-in is definitely a real issue. What's important to note is that LG's 97" G6 model is inferior to its smaller counterparts. Whereas all the other G6 TVs feature LG's latest Primary RGB Tandem 2.0 OLED panel, the 97" version uses a traditional W-OLED panel similar to the one found in the LG B6 TV. It's also dimmer (far dimmer than the QM8L) and caps out at 120Hz refresh rate. In a nutshell, don't expect LG's fantastic "Gallery series image quality" in the 97" variant.

I'd pick the 98" QM8L over a home theater projector

With the QM8L on the market, there's also no telling reason to get a home theater projector unless you're getting a significantly larger screen (120" or bigger). You'd have to spend well over $4,000 to get a projector that can reasonably measure up to the image quality of the QM8L, and even then that would be limited to a completely dark room with an optimized screen that could run you another $1,000 or more. For both movie watching and games at this screen size I'd say go for the TV, and that's coming from someone who's owned a high-end Sony projector for over a decade.

I'd pick the 98" QM8L over TCL's higher-end X11L

TCL makes one additional 98" TV that is technically a superior TV. The 98" X11L is available for a tad under $8,000, or 2.7 times the price of the QM8L. Although both TVs use the new SQD Mini-LED tech, the X11L has far more dimming zones: 20,000 on the X11L compared to 4,000 on the QM8L. That equates to higher peak brightness (10,000nits vs 6,000nits) and more precise colors. It truly is the cream of the crop. However, in real world scenarios, the difference in image quality doesn't justify the massive $5,000 difference in price, unless you have extremely deep pockets.

One of 2026's biggest RPGs has just received its first major discount at Amazon, with The Blood of Dawnwalker now available for $59.49 on PS5 and Xbox as part of the retailer's Prime Big Deal Days sale .

Developed by Rebel Wolves, The Blood of Dawnwalker is a story-driven RPG set in a grim medieval world where, unsurprisingly, vampires have become a rather significant problem. You play as Coen, a young man who is transformed into a vampire and given a limited amount of time to save his family.

That time limit is one of the more interesting ideas at the heart of Dawnwalker. Your human and vampiric abilities give you different ways to approach the world, while the clock is constantly ticking down as you decide how to spend your limited time. It's an RPG where you can't simply do everything, and some of the decisions you make mean accepting that other things will have to wait.

"The Blood of Dawnwalker is my new favorite vampire game and one of the best story-driven RPGs I've played in a long time," wrote IGN's Travis Northup in our 9/10 review .

"The day/night cycle that has you juggling human and vampiric forms is awesome, and the constraints placed on how you spend your limited time ends up being one of the coolest, most wonderfully stressful parts of the adventure."

"Combat has a bit of a learning curve to it, but gets under your skin in all the right ways once you get the hang of it. Combine that with a story filled with memorable characters, gut wrenching decisions, and more endings than I’m ever likely to see, and this adventure kept me firmly in its thrall. Even if you aren’t particularly into the vampire fantasy, this is one that any RPG fan should absolutely not miss."

At $59.49, this isn't the sort of discount that completely transforms the price of a brand-new game, but it's still the first major reduction we've seen for The Blood of Dawnwalker. articles.title: Previous Game Pass Strategy Sent Xbox Into 'Freefall,' CEO Asha Sharma Reportedly Tells Staff
articles.summary: It's no secret that Xbox has had a rough time in 2026. With nearly 2,000 staff cut as part of sweeping layoffs and studio closures, Microsoft's gaming business is in the middle of one of the most significant restructures in video game history. But what led Xbox to this point? According to CEO Asha Sharma, Game Pass played a key role.
articles.body:
It's no secret that Xbox has had a rough time in 2026. With nearly 2,000 staff cut as part of sweeping layoffs and studio closures , Microsoft's gaming business is in the middle of one of the most significant restructures in video game history. But what led Xbox to this point? According to CEO Asha Sharma, Game Pass played a key role.

Today, in an internal memo obtained by Windows Central, Sharma reiterated that Microsoft's Game Pass strategy sent Xbox's balance sheet into "freefall." Jez Corden, who initially reported on this memo, suggested that this was because of "the damage at both ends to Call of Duty and Xbox Game Pass."

It's easy to see why that may be the case. After Xbox bought Activision Blizzard for an eye-watering $69 billion and added Call of Duty to Game Pass, subscription costs skyrocketed, which likely scared away a lot of existing subscribers, and at the same time cut Call of Duty's sales. After all, why spend $70 on the new Call of Duty when you can just buy a month's subscription?

Every Video Game Franchise Xbox Owns After Acquiring Activision Blizzard

But for all the doom and gloom of Game Pass's consequences, Sharma suggested that Xbox is on the way up. In the memo, Sharma said: "We're making the right decisions to reinvest in the business, after an all time low, we've started to return to growth, more than 2 to 3 times what we were, and we expect that to continue."

In the past Sharma has made statements suggesting that Xbox needs to reach more than 1 billion people each day. And while Xbox probably isn't hitting those numbers any time soon, the reported return to growth shows the company is, financially at least, heading in the right direction. It probably doesn't hurt that Blizzard's World of Warcraft: Forever looks like a hit .

It seems like Xbox is going to work to make Game Pass more accessible in the future too, though with a few catches. Last month, there were rumors that Microsoft would be introducing new tiers of Game Pass without the day one launches, both with and without ads. Around the same time, Microsoft also filed a patent that would suspend your game in order to show you an ad for additional game time.

If Microsoft was able to introduce these changes at a low enough price point, it could expand Game Pass by simply being a more affordable way to play games. Those rumors last month suggested the ad-supported tier would be $12.99, which seems high for such a subscription, especially when the base price is $9.99 right now. But if Microsoft was able to lower its asking price, a more limited ad-supported Game Pass could absolutely bring in new players, which does seem to be Sharma's goal.

When Sharma announced the Xbox layoffs in the summer, she admitted that Game Pass had failed to grow as Microsoft had expected.

“Our business today is not healthy,” Sharma said at the time. “We are operating at margins that are 3-10x lower than comparable platform and publishing businesses. We entered Gen 9 with a smaller install base and a higher cost structure. To grow, we bet on Game Pass, multi-platform, and a broader portfolio of content. While those businesses have created meaningful value, they did not grow at the pace we expected. As that happened, our core business weakened, and we added more teams, more investment, and more time, hoping for a better outcome. And now the industry is facing the most severe hardware crisis in its history. We must reset Xbox.”

The Wall Street Journal said that Microsoft had expected Game Pass subscriptions to hit around 77 million this year, but it currently has only about 30 million. As revealed during the FTC vs Microsoft trial of 2023, Microsoft had hoped for 100 million subscribers by 2030, which seems very unlikely at this stage.

One of the first decisions Sharma made after replacing former Xbox boss Phil Spencer was to cut the price of Game Pass and pull Call of Duty out as a day one title. Sharma recently told Bloomberg that Xbox had "been able to reset Game Pass after an eight-month decline." "It’s now returned to growth and expanding retention," she added, "and most importantly, we're starting to get back to being closer to our players and our community."

Still, the future of Game Pass is unclear. Will Microsoft eventually pull all its games out of the subscription as day one launches? Will Bethesda's The Elder Scrolls 6 launch day one on Game Pass? Will the next mainline Halo game? Could we see Game Pass become more like Sony’s PlayStation Plus, which does not launch first-party games day one?

articles.title: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma Shares More Details on Project Helix 'Family of Devices'
articles.summary: As the next generation of consoles looms over the horizon, it's becoming clearer that Microsoft's Project Helix is going to be a whole lineup of gaming devices, rather than one console.
articles.body:
As the next generation of consoles looms over the horizon, it's becoming clearer that Microsoft's Project Helix is going to be a whole lineup of gaming devices, rather than one console.

In a leaked memo sent to staff and obtained by Windows Central , Xbox CEO Asha Sharma described the company's plans for the next generation as involving a family of devices. This isn't the first time she's suggested this, first hinting at it at Gamescom earlier this year. But in the memo, Sharma went into more detail on the range of hardware we can expect.

"We are moving to a family of devices for Gen-10," she reportedly said. "There is not one device that fits all. We will certainly have a great console first, but we also know that many players will be on the go. There are some things that we are the best in the world to manufacture, and there are other things that will we partner on. So, we will be sharing more about that as our plans develop. The operating system is starting to look really good. We're very excited about this."

Anyone who's watched Microsoft's hardware strategy over the last few years shouldn't be too surprised by this. After all, the current generation of consoles launched with two seperate boxes, the Xbox Series X and cheaper and less powerful Series S, with different users in mind. Then, last year, the company partnered with Asus to launch the ROG Xbox Ally X , which is still one of the best handheld gaming PCs on the market.

It's too early to know what exactly Microsoft's next-generation consoles are going to look like, but Sharma's statement suggests there will be at least one core console in the family. That will likely be the successor to the Xbox Series X, and will be the focus of Xbox's partnership with AMD . After the success of the Xbox Ally and Xbox Ally X, though, I'd expect a whole lineup of Xbox-branded gaming PCs.

Microsoft is no stranger to partnering with hardware manufacturers; after all, it's been doing so with Windows for decades. The company already has the connections to branch out, so I'd expect anything from more handheld gaming PCs to even Xbox-branded laptops and desktop PCs.

I'm particularly interested in seeing how the operating system plays out. Windows 11 is almost universally the worst part of every handheld gaming PC that uses it, and while the Xbox Full Screen Experience has vastly improved over the last year, there's still a lot of room for improvement, especially if Xbox is expecting it to have the same no-brainer approach that modern console UIs have.

If Microsoft is hoping to embrace the PC gaming side of Xbox, though, it'll need to lean on more than just the Xbox app on Windows. I don't know about you, but that's not the first storefront I gravitate towards, even on my Ally X. But Sharma seems aware of this too. According to Jez Corden, who broke the story on this memo, it also mentioned Xbox PC and Battle.net, and specifically how Blizzard's launcher is "almost on-par with Steam for user retention."

Now that Xbox owns Blizzard and can likely just put whatever it wants on that store, I'd expect the company to launch more games there. Blizzard's fan base is notoriously fickle, however, and the launcher also has a problem where as soon as any game is added to the store, it shows up in your favorites bar. There's real opportunity for Xbox, which is likely why The Witcher 3 Remastered just launched there, but Microsoft will have to play a careful hand.

Sharma also seemed to acknowledge that in her note, saying: "We will do it the right way for those communities," but this is just another thing Xbox needs to iron out with its user experience before it launches a next-generation suite of hardware.

But, if Xbox is able to work out those kinks and deliver a Windows 11 (or 12) experience that's as easy to use as the Xbox Series X, (or let's be real, SteamOS), Project Helix could end up defining the next console generation.

articles.title: Two mystery PlayStation products have leaked — one might be a PlayStation Portal OLED
articles.summary: The Wi-Fi Alliance recently certified two unannounced PlayStation products of some kind that could be updates to the PlayStation Portal.
articles.body: Is Sony about to announce a new PlayStation Portal game streaming handheld? The Wi-Fi Alliance recently certified two unannounced PlayStation products of some kind, and the certification documents indicate that they could be updates to the PlayStation Portal, which might mean we’re getting the OLED screen rumored earlier this year. The two devices, which are classified as “Gaming Console/Peripherals,” have model numbers of CFI-Y2000 and CFI-Y2105, which sound like a clear step up from the CFI-Y1001 model number for the currently available Portal. The docs say that the new models run on Android 15, which further indicates that they might be Portals; the current model also runs Android. (The PS5 home console, on the other hand, runs a custom OS.) While Sony is expected to eventually announce a PlayStation handheld that natively plays PS5 games on next-gen AMD graphics, its PlayStation Portal streams games instead, either from your home PlayStation or from Sony’s cloud. That can make for a far more affordable device, something Sony itself pointed out this June: “Cloud streaming also requires minimal memory, making it an increasingly attractive low-cost thin client device in the current market environment where memory prices are rising.” The new gadgets don’t look like they’re getting dramatically improved Wi-Fi for streaming, though: they’re certified for 1x1 2.4GHz and 5GHz Wi-Fi, but not 6GHz and seemingly without more antennas. There’s not much more to glean from the certification docs, unfortunately — I’ve embedded them at the end of this article, if you want to see them for yourself — and PlayStation didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment. But as reported by VideoCardz, hardware leaker KeplerL2 said earlier this year that Sony was working on “another version” of the Portal for this year that would be an “OLED version.” The original Portal, which has an 8-inch LCD screen, launched in late 2023.

articles.title: Lanterns Needs to Become a Very Different Series in Season 2
articles.summary: As much as we loved Lanterns Season 1, it needs to fundamentally reinvent itself for Season 2. Here's why the DCU series can't rest on its laurels.
articles.body:
There’s no doubt that Lanterns has been a big success for DC and HBO. The series successfully restored faith in James Gunn’s DCU after the misfire that was Supergirl . It also established a pivotal new hero in Aaron Pierre’s John Stewart, paving the way for the newly minted Green Lantern to appear in Gunn’s Man of Tomorrow .

While HBO has yet to formally greenlight Lanterns Season 2, it sounds like work is already well underway on writing the next season . That said, the prospect of more Lanterns has us feeling mixed emotions. As much as we want more of the series, we also recognize that it needs to profoundly change in Season 2. Here’s why Lanterns can’t simply deliver more of the same when it returns.

Can Lanterns Work Without Kyle Chandler’s Hal Jordan?

Most Lanterns fans would probably agree that the show’s biggest selling point throughout Season 1 was the dynamic between Pierre’s John and Kyle Chandler’s Hal Jordan. Seeing the idealistic young John butt heads with the cantankerous, grizzled Hal never gets old. The DCU’s casting game has really been on-point so far, and nowhere is that more true than with the two Lanterns leads.

There’s just one problem - the show killed off half of that all-important equation. The series premiere closed with the reveal that Hal had been murdered in 2026. Thanks to the frequent flashbacks and the presence of Hal’s holographic backup (or “Halogram”), Season 1 still managed to feature the character prominently in most episodes.

But that likely won’t be the case for Season 2. The season finale delivers a final death for Hal when John finally claims the ring for himself and recharges it. The act of becoming a Green Lantern purges all traces of Hal’s consciousness from the ring. John has now embraced his heroic destiny, but that leaves him without his grumpy mentor going forward.

That’s a major issue for the series. Again, the central conflict between Hal and John was a huge driving force of Season 1 and the biggest reason to tune in each and every week. As it stands, the series lagged a bit in Episode 6 when Chandler stepped out of the spotlight. How can Lanterns hope to move forward when Chandler will presumably be out of the picture entirely? How can it fill that void?

Given how stoic and composed John is, he really needs a partner who can serve as a foil and fill those quiet spaces with emotion. If Hal Jordan can’t be that foil any longer, then someone else needs to rise to the challenge. Maybe that involves making Nathan Fillion’s Guy Gardner a more active member of the cast. I’d certainly like to see that dysfunctional relationship explored now that John has effectively muscled his way into taking over jurisdiction of Earth.

Or maybe the series needs to flip the script and turn John into the mentor to another aspiring Lantern. The comics certainly have no shortage of potential candidates, from Kyle Rayner to Jo Mullein to Simon Baz. Given John’s status as a Lantern who embraces fear rather than suppresses it, I’d be particularly interested in seeing him shepherd Jessica Cruz, a Lantern struggling to overcome her crippling anxiety disorder.

It’s also worth pointing out that the series did leave itself a couple of outs when it comes to bringing back Hal. For one thing, a lot has been made of John’s ability to create constructs that persist even when he’s not wearing the ring. Is it possible that the Halogram could continue to exist even after the ring itself is purged?

For another, Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen) specifically tells John in Episode 8 that he knows a way to resurrect Hal. That revelation is never followed up, but it could be a seed for Season 2. Some fans have speculated that Sinestro is working to establish his corps of Yellow Lanterns and intends to resurrect Hal as the host for the fear entity Parallax. It would certainly be interesting to see Hal return not as the grumpy elder statesman, but as a full-blown villain waging war on the Green Lantern Corps (a thing that actually happened in the comics).

One thing is clear. However the revamped writers’ room opts to move forward in Season 2, they can’t simply coast by with the same formula that made Season 1 such a hit. Either a new character needs to step up to fill the hole left by Hal, or Hal himself needs to return in a very different form. As great as the Hal/John dynamic in Season 1 was, the series can’t simply move forward with more of the same.

From Murder Mystery to Superhero Adventure

On that note, the original Lanterns announcement turned a lot of heads when it was revealed that the series wouldn’t be a traditional Green Lantern adaptation, but a murder mystery set on Earth. Not everyone was thrilled at the prospect of a Green Lantern show that shares more in common with the likes of True Detective than the sci-fi-infused source material. And while Season 1 made a pretty strong case for that approach in the end, there are still those yearning for a more faithful Green Lantern adventure.

Season 2 needs to throw a bone to those fans. It’s not enough to simply replicate the formula of Season 1. Lanterns can’t settle simply for pairing John with a new trainee and forcing them to unravel a conspiracy in another small town. Doing so will only make the series feel stale and force Season 2 to exist in the shadow of its predecessor.

And ultimately, Season 1’s murder mystery wasn’t really where the show found its appeal. It only worked because that mystery provided the perfect vehicle for John to chafe against his upbringing and learn how to be a hero who embraces fear rather than ignores it. That arc is done. Now it’s time to see what happens when John becomes the hero he was always meant to be.

That means the series needs to lean more into the larger-than-life Green Lantern elements that Season 1 downplayed so much. Yes, we suspect the ethos of the show will always reflect Hal’s line, “Knowing when to use [the ring] is the whole ballgame, Junior.” But the time has come to let that ring shine a little more. We need to see the Green Lantern in action and exploring his amazing new powers.

Granted, that’s going to present some steep challenges for the show to overcome. As much as the grounded, Earth-centric approach of Season 1 was a dramatic and stylistic choice, it was also one borne of practicality. It’s not cheap to build a show around a cosmic superhero who can literally create anything his mind can envision. There’s a reason the show’s various alien characters almost invariably opted to disguise themselves as humans.

It’s enough to make you wonder if the path forward for this franchise shouldn’t be more television, but a pivot to a big-budget film. We will get a taste of that when Pierre reprises his role in 2027’s Man of Tomorrow . But for better or worse, John’s path in the DCU seems to involve more small-screen adventures.

This means there’s a delicate balance the writers of Season 2 will have to strike. They need to find ways of capturing the scope of John’s new lot in life. He’s a Green Lantern in the prime of his career, not an embittered, aging old kook turning over rocks in a remote Nebraskan town. At the same time, the show has to build a storyline that’s feasible and doable on an HBO budget. Not an easy task.

DC Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

I suspect the path forward for Lanterns is going to involve elevating a minor figure from Season 1. The time has come for Sinestro to abandon his role as the show’s Hannibal Lecter-esque figure and step fully into the forefront. As it is, I found Season 1’s lack of focus on Sinestro a little frustrating, but there’s certainly room to make up for lost time in Season 2.

As it is, a lot of Season 1’s loose ends seem to revolve around Sinestro in one way or another. He formed an alliance of sorts with Noah (Shea Pritchard), a character whom we now know is the universe’s last surviving Manhunter. Noah now seems trapped on a precipice, unsure of whether he should give in to his programming and wage war on the Guardians or become the force for good John believes he can be. There’s also the aforementioned tease that Sinestro knows how to resurrect Hal.

Right now, the character is trapped in a very literal form of limbo, still marooned on the dead alien world where John and the Halogram found him. But that can easily change. Season 2 can and should explore what happens when Sinestro is finally freed and resumes his own campaign against the Guardians.

Season 1 alluded to a rich history between Sinestro and Hal. We know the two were very close, right up until the day Sinestro launched an uprising against the Guardians and Hal was forced to rein in his old mentor. That act seemingly broke Hal in a profound way, and he was never the same afterward.

But for all that Sinestro is the most pivotal Green Lantern villain in the comics, there’s a lot that the DCU has yet to delve into. This version of Sinestro is only beginning to appreciate the power of fear. We don’t know if he’s managed to forge a Yellow Lantern ring yet, much less spearhead the creation of an entire Corps. It’s high time we see the Sinestro Corps in live-action.

Ultimately, if Lanterns is in need of a character to fill the void left by Hal, maybe Sinestro is the right man for the job. We have a sense of the powerful bond that linked Sinestro and Hal, but what about Sinestro and John? Are they destined to be enemies, or is there a sort of kinship that exists, given that John himself is willing to embrace fear? And how does Noah fit into this growing rivalry? If there’s a path forward for Lanterns, Sinestro may be the one to light the way.

What do you want to see out of Lanterns Season 2? Let us know in the comments below.

articles.title: GTA 6 Fans Theorize Jason May Be the Franchise's First Neurodivergent Protagonist
articles.summary: GTA 6 fans have begun to speculate over whether or not Jason is the franchise's first outwardly neurodivergent protagonist.
articles.body:
GTA 6 fans have begun to speculate over whether or not Jason is the franchise's first outwardly neurodivergent protagonist.

In a recent interview with Love magazine, longtime Rockstar Games writer Rupert Humphries spoke about how the team designed Jason and Lucia's personalities. One specific comment that fans have latched on to is one where Humphries describes Jason as being "wired differently."

"We didn’t want to make any kind of statement with Jason’s backstory," Humphries said in response to a question over whether or not Jason is a commentary on social class. "It needs to be understood that he takes the measures he does — drug trafficking and becoming a bank robber, etc. — because of his material circumstances. But a lot of this is up to the player to decide whether he needs to do that, or if it’s a choice he makes because he’s wired differently from other people."

Fans have used this as a jumping-off point to reflect on some of the footage we've seen of Jason up to this point. During the extended gameplay reveal in August, fans were quick to point out that Jason is often seen missing social cues. At one point, he does a handshake with a character and raises his arm out to keep it going, only to quickly put it back down when he realizes the other person is no longer paying attention. He can also be seen avoiding eye contact with some characters and expressing anxiety over a meeting with a friend, noting he's more comfortable with a gun.

Some fans have used this to speculate that Jason is actually neurodivergent. Some neurodivergent traits that he may portray are social fatigue (being drained by small talk) and masking (copying other people's behaviors in an effort to fit in). It's also possible that Jason is simply a very reserved, quiet guy. He's ex-military, so he may just be more restrained and disciplined in his behavior.

We likely won't get too much more insight into Jason, outside of maybe one more trailer, before launch. GTA 6 is less than 45 days from release now and Rockstar is preparing a massive marketing campaign. On top of murals and ads around major cities such as New York and Miami , Rockstar will also take over the Miami Heat for one night only and rebrand them as the Vice City Heat . They will play a regular-season NBA game against the Bucks on a Vice City-themed court in Miami on November 18.

articles.title: Sega Community Relations Director Speaks Out After Sonic Discord Goes Wild
articles.summary: Sega created a Discord server just for Sonic fans — and it wasn’t long until it descended into chaos, forcing its moderators to take action in an admittedly unexpected, if somewhat amusing, turn of events.
articles.body:
Sega created a Discord server just for Sonic fans — and it wasn’t long until it descended into chaos, forcing its moderators to take sweeping action in an admittedly unexpected, if somewhat amusing, turn of events.

On October 5, Sonic rolled out an official Discord server for fans of the blue blur to mix and mingle. As with most large servers, the Sonic team preemptively laid out rules for its community to follow (which, hilariously, included a bit about AI-generated art involving an Eggman dating simulator), but it wasn’t long before those rules were flagrantly flaunted.

Mere hours after launching, things got so hectic that the moderators removed most users’ ability to chat, locking it behind a members-only role and requiring fans to boost the server — and while order was eventually restored and these restrictions were mostly lifted, the ordeal left a lasting impression on the internet.

Sonic the Hedgehog x Godzilla #2 Preview Gallery

According to firsthand reports of fans who were in the server at the time of its launch, there was some pretty wild fanart getting shared, on top of other rule-breaking behavior that needs no description. (We imagine you get the gist.)

Now that the dust has settled, one of the minds behind creating this server has spoken out. Aaron Webber, the director of strategy, studio, and community relations at Sega of Japan, gave curious onlookers a glimpse behind the curtain at what actually happened and how the moderation team managed to handle such a massive influx of fans all at once.

In a tweet thread, Webber disagreed with framing the ordeal as chaotic, saying that, while there was certainly a lot of action that needed to be taken straight away, it wasn’t nearly as bad as some fans were making it out to be.

“The very start was pretty wild, and this is normal when over 30,000 people arrive and all excitedly want to talk. The mods have been doing a heroic job keeping the server clean during that window, and since. Big props to all of them,” he began.

“You may see cherry-picked screens of bad actors trying to cause havoc, but these were all swiftly removed and banned. One of the key ways the server is kept clean so quickly is through the automatic filters, which are very strict right now,” he continued.

Webber went on to say that the moderation team is working to unban those wrongly affected and is currently fine-tuning its ban system. He also assured fans that they will soon be able to type in the chat once spam restrictions have been reworked.

The humorous Discord debacle has drawn quite a few eyes to the Sonic fanbase, who are eagerly waiting for more news on the next Sonic movie. The fourth film is slated to release on March 19, 2027. All we currently know about it is that Amy Rose and Metal Sonic are supposed to be involved, but anything beyond that has been shrouded in mystery. But hey, at least the fans can chat about it in the official Discord together now!

Every Fortnite Festival season includes its own mix of free songs, while players can also buy songs to keep permanently. articles.title: Death Stranding Movie Gets Update as Director Scouts Beautiful Filming Locations in Iceland
articles.summary: The Death Stranding movie appears to be ramping up to production, as director Michael Sarnoski and cinematographer Pat Scola share a beautiful view from location scouting.
articles.body:
The Death Stranding movie appears to be ramping up to production, as director Michael Sarnoski and cinematographer Pat Scola recently shared a beautiful view from location scouting.

Death Stranding director Michael Sarnoski is currently in Iceland scouting for locations that can be used for the film. He shared a selfie of himself wearing a Death Stranding T-shirt and also reposted a video from his cinematographer, Pat Scola, showcasing gorgeous Icelandic scenery featuring waterfalls and plenty of moss. It is a pretty breathtaking view, and one that perfectly replicates the kind of landscape you'd find in Death Stranding, albeit with a bit more sun.

Whether or not this exact location will be used in the film remains to be seen, but it does show that the creative team behind the film understands the game's aesthetic. It's also great to see that they're going to be shooting on location, instead of relying exclusively on soundstages and CG backdrops. Sarnoski revealed earlier this summer that he plans to shoot the Death Stranding film next year in Iceland and Northern Ireland .

Director Michael Sarnoski is on a location scout in Iceland for the #DeathStranding film produced by A24 and Square Peg — NV (@naven0m) October 6, 2026

Director Michael Sarnoski is on a location scout in Iceland for the #DeathStranding film produced by A24 and Square Peg

Sarnoski's Death Stranding will be a new, original story set within the world of the game. It has the full backing and involvement of series creator Hideo Kojima and will be produced in conjunction with A24. As a result, you can expect a new cast of characters, but Sarnoski has teased that familiar faces from the games may appear, as well . The film also comes at an interesting time, as Kojima has said he's uninterested in helming a third Death Stranding game , but would let someone else make it based on a concept he created. He's finding other ways to flesh out the world through both this film and other media, including an anime.

There's currently no release date for the Death Stranding film, but a 2028 release date may not be out of the question depending on when it starts shooting next year. Cast details are also currently under wraps, but with production ramping up, we will presumably hear more on that front soon. Norman Reedus has already expressed interest in reprising his role as Sam Porter Bridges in the film , but his involvement has yet to be announced.
